---
title: "Resources"
order: 54
---

- [FDA guidance: *Blood Establishment Computer System Validation in the User's Facility*](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/blood-establishment-computer-system-validation-users-facility)
  — the guidance page for the document this course has quoted from every module, including this
  one's III.G interface and legacy-conversion bullets and III.J. Use it to confirm you're reading
  the current, final version (CBER, April 2013) and to pull the full PDF if you want more context
  around any quote in this lesson.

- [21 CFR 211.68, Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/211.68)
  — the input/output-accuracy paragraph, (b), this module quotes for the first time in this
  course. Use it to read (a) and (b) together: the requirement to validate the system at all, and
  the requirement to validate what crosses its edges.

- [21 CFR 606.165, Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.165)
  — distribution and receipt records, applied here to the electronic shipment-data interface to
  Riverside General Hospital. Use it when you need the exact (b)/(c) field list this module tested
  the interface against.

- [21 CFR 11.10, Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/11.10)
  — the full closed-system controls list, including (h), device checks, requoted briefly here
  after module 5 deferred its depth to this lesson. Use it to see (h) next to (d), (f), and (g),
  the controls module 5 built out in full.

- **[HL7 Tutorial for Beginners: How to Read and Build an HL7 v2
  Message](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RjIDeic78qo)** (Sidharth Ramesh, from oEmbed
  `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson. General healthcare-integration training on
  HL7 v2 message structure, not blood-center- or FDA-specific; use it to be able to read what an
  interface error file or a malformed test message actually contains. Verified embeddable via
  YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA: Data Integrity and Compliance With Drug CGMP, Questions and
  Answers](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/data-integrity-and-compliance-drug-cgmp-questions-and-answers)**
  — FDA guidance (guidance tier, written for drug CGMP, not blood) on data integrity expectations for
  computerized systems. Read it as FDA's plain-language statement of the properties this lesson
  calls complete, correct, and on time, and as a preview of what `data-integrity-and-records` will
  go deeper on. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA: Part 11, Electronic Records; Electronic Signatures, Scope and
  Application](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/part-11-electronic-records-electronic-signatures-scope-and-application)**
  — the 2003 guidance module 5 used for its enforcement-discretion list, which includes the device
  checks of 11.10(h) this lesson applies to interfaces. Read it to see (h) in the context of the
  controls FDA says it still intends to enforce. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Microsoft Learn: Service Bus dead-letter
  queues](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-dead-letter-queues)**
  — a vendor explainer of the dead-letter queue concept this lesson maps onto FDA's "interface
  error file." Use it to sharpen the ITSM side of the bridge: why unprocessable messages are
  parked and who has to look at them. It is generic cloud documentation, not a regulatory source.
  Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[ICCBBA](https://iccbba.org/)** — the organization that maintains the product-code reference
  tables behind boundary 3 (and DEV-1147). Use it to see what ICCBBA publishes and how
  implementation and table updates are described by the source itself. Verified loading via `curl`
  on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
